A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DeepImageSearch/DISBench work and provide readable main text, figures, tables, and Appendices A-E. Content can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original DISBench agent and retrieval evaluations, component ablations, test-time scaling, error analyses, and qualitative experimental traces.

after.justification: V2 retains the original experimental results in Tables 1-3, the scaling and error-analysis plots, and Appendix E.

M1.justification: Section 4 revises compressed memory from session/working summaries to global/local/tool-use summaries, adding explicit failure-history retention and an image-count trigger. This is a limited reported procedural revision, but v2 Appendix D.2 still specifies the original two-component design, leaving the implemented variant uncertain.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same YFCC100M-derived DISBench coverage: 122 queries, 57 users, 109,467 photos, and intra-event/inter-event retrieval tasks. Removing the geographic map does not establish a change in the underlying population.

E2.justification: Tables 1-3 retain the same ten agent backbones, Qwen3-VL-Embedding 2B/8B and Seed-1.6-Embedding retrieval comparisons, and component-removal variants. The newly cited works are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Sections 5.1 and Appendix D.4 retain the same evaluation metrics, 30-turn limit, 128K-token context limit, default temperatures, and retrieval/viewing limits. No revised experimental protocol is reported; whether the revised Section 4 memory description applies to these experiments remains unresolved.

E4.justification: Appendix C.4 loses the supplementary characterization of photo locations through v1 Figure 7 and its accompanying geographic-coverage discussion. The tool/memory ablations, test-time scaling, four-model error analysis, and two Appendix E cases are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same parallel-run counts in the scaling study and annotation agreement reporting, including IoU 0.91. Neither adds seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or a changed uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: All matched performance values in Tables 1-3, scaling curves, error percentages, and Appendix E traces are unchanged. The limited loss is the empirical geographic point distribution shown in v1 Figure 7 and its accompanying coverage summary; no performance gain or loss is reported.

T1.justification: The context-aware set-retrieval formulation, memory-graph definitions, and Appendix C sampling algorithm remain unchanged. Neither version introduces additional theorems, proofs, or formal derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about context-dependent retrieval, DISBench construction, the ImageSeeker baseline, and current models' reasoning limitations.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 newly qualifies the embedding comparison as demonstrating DISBench's need for cross-image reasoning, rather than supporting replacement of embedding retrievers by agents generally. Appendix B's substantive limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V1's separate code, dataset, and leaderboard links become a single repository entry point in v2, changing the supplied access instructions without establishing resource withdrawal. Most implementation details remain unchanged, and Appendix D.2 is not reconciled with the revised main-text memory specification.

R1.justification: V2 adds Naaman et al. (2004) and Whittaker et al. (2010) to motivate contextual personal-photo retrieval, plus MR2-Bench and MC-Search in related work. These are limited additions; the central novelty positioning is retained.

P1.justification: Edits are localized: expanded personal-album motivation, a rewritten memory paragraph, a renamed and qualified Section 5.3, grammatical corrections, conference publication text, and acknowledgments. The overall section and appendix structure is retained.

P2.justification: V2 removes the geographic map, relocates the dataset chart and results tables, swaps the numbering of the scaling and error plots, and expands their captions. Front-page links become a footnote, and the second qualitative case spans pages; the retained displays otherwise preserve their designs.

improvement.justification: The added references and Section 5.3 qualification improve framing, but v2 introduces a reproducibility inconsistency: Section 4 describes three memory tiers while Appendix D.2 retains two. It also removes geographic-distribution evidence. The PDFs do not resolve which memory design underlies the retained results, so the benefits and harms do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
